Here, we show that all ${\mathrm{CFT}}_{3}\text{ }\mathrm{s}$, inclu… [Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 221601] Published Mon Nov 23, 2026 — Andrew Strominger, Hongji Wei — Physical Review Letters

item.title: Correlation functions of 2D critical models via a KPZ relation for conformal blocks
item.description: The Knizhnik--Polyakov--Zamolodchikov (KPZ) relation allows scaling exponents of two-dimensional (2D) critical systems to be derived from their counterparts in Liouville quantum gravity. We extend this framework to correlation functions based on an integral inversion relation between Virasoro conformal blocks with complementary central charges $c$ and $26-c$. We demonstrate this method in various models by deriving the 2-point disk correlation from their quantum counterpart and the KPZ relation. Results on critical loop models were previously known, but our method is robust enough to include many scenarios previously unsolved, such as the Fuzzy Potts model. Our approach is complementary to… — Gefei Cai, Shengzhi Jin, Xin Sun, Baojun Wu — arXiv math.AP / CA / PR / DS / arXiv math-ph / hep-th

item.title: Holographic probes and Krylov complexity on asymptotically Lifshitz rotating black branes
item.description: We study two types of holographic probes on a five-dimensional, asymptotically Lifshitz, rotating black hole. This geometry solves the field equations of Einstein gravity coupled to a dilaton, two axionic scalars, and a Maxwell doublet, supplemented by two vector doublets that enter the action through a parity-odd, Chern-Simons-like combination, as recently found in \cite{Bravo-Gaete:2026bdq}. This spacetime provides a concrete bottom-up arena to explore the imprints of rotation on probes in non-relativistic holography. First, we compute the holographic static quark-antiquark potential following the standard prescription that relates this boundary observable to the on shell-action of a… — Moises Bravo-Gaete, Mariano Chernicoff, Benjamin Mellado, Julio Oliva, Maria Guadalupe Olmos Andrade — arXiv gr-qc / astro-ph.CO / hep-ph / arXiv math-ph / hep-th

item.title: Exponential integrability of SLE Minkowski content
item.description: Let $0<\kappa<8$, $d=1+\kappa/8$, and $q=2/(2-d)$. Let $\mu$ be the $d$-dimensional Minkowski content measure of either chordal $\mathrm{SLE}_\kappa$ in $\mathbb H$ from $0$ to $\infty$ or two-sided whole-plane $\mathrm{SLE}_\kappa$ through $0$. We prove that there exist constants $c_\kappa,C_\kappa\in(0,\infty)$ such that \[ \mathbb E\exp\left\{c_\kappa\left(\frac{\mu(D)}{(\operatorname{diam} D)^d}\right)^q\right\}\le C_\kappa \] for every deterministic bounded Borel set $D$ of positive diameter in the corresponding domain. The exponent $q$ in this moment bound is optimal in both settings. We also show that, almost surely, $\mu(B(z,r))=O\bigl(r^d(\log(1/r))^{1/q}\bigr)$ as $r\downarrow0$… — Dapeng Zhan — arXiv math.AP / CA / PR / DS

item.title: Teichm\"uller spaces with conical singularities and Virasoro coadjoint orbits
item.description: We study Teichm\"uller spaces of hyperbolic \(0\)-metrics on a disk with ideal boundary and a marked point carrying a conical singularity with angle $\theta = 2\pi \beta$. For all $\beta>0$, we show that $\rm{Teich}^{\beta}(\overline{\mathbb D})\cong S^1\backslash \rm{Diff}(S^1)$, and we construct natural closed 2-forms $\omega_\beta$ induced by the Atiyah-Bott construction. For non-integer $\beta$, the form $\omega_\beta$ is symplectic, and one can identify $\rm{Teich}^{\beta}(\overline{\mathbb D})$ with the corresponding elliptic Virasoro coadjoint orbit. For positive integers $\beta=n$, $\omega_\beta$ is presymplectic, and it descends to the Kirillov-Kostant-Souriau symplectic form on… — Anton Alekseev, Rea Dalipi, Samson Shatashvili — arXiv math-ph / hep-th / arXiv math.GT / AT / SG / DG

item.title: Moonshine Conjecture Formalized
item.description: The celebrated and intimidating Moonshine Conjecture has now been formalized in Lean. This achievement might suggest that, once a sufficiently large library compiles, the principal mathematical work is complete. This paper tells a less optimistic story. During our formalization project, we repeatedly encountered two problems that a formally checked proof alone does not settle: (1) whether the formal statements actually express the mathematics we humans expect, and (2) how that meaning survives as the repositories and their dependencies evolve. We argue that there is no magic pill that turns a large agent-produced library into mathematics a community can trust. Even after the proofs are… — Jin-Cheng Guu — arXiv cs.AI / cs.LG / cs.LO (AI for math) / arXiv math-ph / hep-th

item.title: Virasoro operators for relative Gromov--Witten theory
item.description: Let $D$ be a smooth divisor in a smooth projective variety $X$. We construct relative Virasoro operators acting on the relative descendant potential of $(X,D)$. Each operator is the logarithmic Virasoro operator of $(X,D)$ plus a boundary correction determined only by $D$ and its normal bundle in $X$. Assuming the Virasoro conjecture for $D$, we prove that the relative constraints are equivalent to the absolute constraints for $X$. Under the same assumption, we establish compatibility with the degeneration formula for two-component projective semistable degenerations satisfying a completeness condition. Consequently, the Virasoro conjecture for the two components and the gluing divisor… — Shuai Guo, Longting Wu, Lei You — arXiv math.NT / AG / RT / arXiv math-ph / hep-th

item.title: Lie Algebra Cohomology and Seiberg-Witten Theory
item.description: We compute the algebra of perturbative holomorphic-topological local operators of pure $\mathcal N=2$ gauge theory with gauge group $SU(2)$, proving a conjecture of the author: it is the Poisson vertex algebra generated by a Virasoro element $X$ of central charge zero and an odd primary $Y$ of weight three, subject only to $X^2=0$. Equivalently, we compute the relative Lie algebra cohomology $H^*(\mathfrak{sl}_2[z,w]/(w^2),\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ and the self-Ext groups of the unit in the coherent Satake category for $SL_2$ and $PGL_2$. The proof uses factorization on configuration spaces of points on the affine line, a depth argument, and two deformations of the coefficient algebra $\mathbb… — Ahsan Z. Khan — arXiv math.NT / AG / RT / arXiv math-ph / hep-th

item.title: Scalar perturbations in extremal Reissner-Nordstr\"om geometry: new methods at work
item.description: We study scalar radiation emitted by a particle moving along a circular orbit around a four-dimensional extremal Reissner-Nordstr\"om black hole. In particular, we calculate the energy fluxes carried by scalar waves to infinity and across the event horizon, as well as the scalar self-force acting on the particle, and express all these quantities as post-Newtonian expansions. Our results for the energy fluxes are in agreement with previous numerical findings in the literature. To solve the radial wave equation, we employ and test two distinct analytic approaches: the first is the so-called \textit{kink method}, a novel alternative stemming from quantum integrability and the second is the… — Giorgio Di Russo, Davide Fioravanti, Francesco Olivi, Marco Rossi — arXiv gr-qc / astro-ph.CO / hep-ph / arXiv math-ph / hep-th

item.title: Large-scale regularity theory for optimal $p-$transport maps and application to concentration in the matching problem
item.description: We consider the random bipartite matching problem between two independent families of uniformly distributed points in dimension three and higher, for the cost given by the $p$-th power of the distance. We show that, up to logarithmic factors, every moment of the displacement of the optimal matching is of the order of the typical interparticle distance. This is a higher integrability, or Calder\'on--Zygmund type, estimate for optimal transport, and it settles, on the torus and up to logarithmic factors, a recent conjecture of D'Achille, Mattesini and the third author. As a consequence, we obtain concentration of the matching cost around its mean for every $p\ge2$. The proof combines a… — Michael Goldman, Lukas Koch, Dario Trevisan — arXiv math.AP / CA / PR / DS

item.title: Nonzero central quotients of the Virasoro enveloping algebra are simple
item.description: We prove a conjecture of Petukhov and Sierra that the central quotient $\mathrm{U}(\mathrm{Vir})/(z-c)$ of the universal enveloping algebra of the Virasoro algebra is simple for all $c \neq 0$. We extend the result to the $N=1$ super-Virasoro algebras. Our proof reveals a new connection between enveloping algebras and polynomial identity algebras. Although the enveloping algebra itself does not satisfy a polynomial identity, the adjoint action on each filtered piece does satisfy a standard identity. In particular, the Witt algebra $W$, as an adjoint module over itself, satisfies the standard identity $\mathrm{St}_4$, whereas $\mathrm{Vir}$ fails by a nonzero multiple of the central charge… — Tuan Anh Pham, Haijun Tan — arXiv math.NT / AG / RT

item.title: Global large-data strong solutions to the 2D barotropic compressible Navier-Stokes equations with linear bulk viscosity
item.description: This paper concerns the global well-posedness of the two-dimensional(2D) compressible Navier--Stokes equations with density-dependent bulk viscosity and far-field vacuum. We consider the constitutive laws \(P(\rho)=\rho^\gamma\), with \(\gamma>1\), and \(\lambda(\rho)=\rho\), for which the bulk viscosity degenerates in vacuum. Under suitable regularity and weighted integrability assumptions on the initial data, and assuming only that the total mass is positive, we establish the existence and uniqueness of global strong solutions without any restriction on the size of the initial energy or any radial symmetry assumption. The central difficulty is to derive an upper bound for the density on… — Qian Li, Zhilei Liang, Zhuan Ye — arXiv math.AP / CA / PR / DS

item.title: Disk 2-point functions for conformal loop ensemble: a derivation from the SLE loop CFT
item.description: We give a derivation of the bulk two-point functions of two-dimensional critical loop models in the disk based on conformal loop ensembles (CLE) and the conformal field theory of SLE loop measures developed by Baverez--Jego. Combining local Ward identities with the spectral resolution of the SLE-loop CFT, we express the two-point functions as contour integrals involving known CLE three-point structure constants and Virasoro conformal blocks. With a suitable choice of contour, these integrals are absolutely convergent and provide a unified representation of a broad class of correlation functions, valid for both irrational and rational central charges. For irrational central charges… — Shengzhi Jin, Xin Sun, Baojun Wu — arXiv math.AP / CA / PR / DS / arXiv math-ph / hep-th

item.title: Horizon dynamical entropies and phase space topology
item.description: We study phase space topologies induced by infinite-dimensional norms as a means to solve the problem of 'integrability' of Hamiltonian generators corresponding to diffeomorphisms of a null hypersurface, with the specific goal in mind to compare different prescriptions for the dynamical entropy of black holes, which replaces the area in non-stationary regimes. We first show that for a scalar field, there exists a family of norms that would provide integrability for different polarizations. We then show that a single member of this family applies to the gravitational field, and it is given by the Sobolev norm already considered in the literature. The obstruction to the other candidates lies… — Matteo Bruno, Simone Speziale — arXiv gr-qc / astro-ph.CO / hep-ph / arXiv math-ph / hep-th

item.title: Scalar-tensor interactions selected through their first-order thermodynamic dynamics
item.description: We investigate the restrictive capability of first-order thermodynamics on scalar-tensor gravity. Starting from a general action containing nonlinear curvature dependence, an Einstein-tensor-Hessian coupling, and independent quadratic and cubic scalar-Hessian interactions, we derive the complete effective-fluid quantities. Simultaneously imposing Eckart's heat-conduction and shear-viscosity equations, while accounting for cancellations between interactions, substantially reduces the original operator basis and determines the geometric shear viscosity. Retaining the complete heat-conduction law, we establish an integrability condition that constrains the nonlinear Hessian interactions… — David S. Pereira — arXiv gr-qc / astro-ph.CO / hep-ph / arXiv math-ph / hep-th

item.title: Non-formality of prefactorization algebras
item.description: We construct a Poisson bracket on the cohomology of locally constant prefactorization algebras on $\mathbb{R}^m$ that provides an obstruction to formality in every dimension $m\geqslant 2$. Our construction combines colored obstruction sequences to formality with linking spheres and generalizes the two-dimensional bracket of Bruinsma, Schenkel, and Vicedo. We use it to extend their non-formality theorem for Lie algebra factorization envelopes to all higher dimensions. We also establish new non-formality results for factorization envelopes of Lie algebras, their compactifications and generalizations to $L_\infty$-algebras, free BF-type theories, higher abelian Chern-Simons theories and… — Coline Emprin, Alex Takeda — arXiv math-ph / hep-th / arXiv math.GT / AT / SG / DG

item.title: Late-time OTOCs in Toda conformal field theory
item.description: We study late-time out-of-time-order correlators (OTOCs) of semi-degenerate primary fields in two-dimensional $A_{N-1}$ Toda conformal field theory. In Liouville theory ($N=2$), we find that the OTOC decays as $t^{-3/2}$ when the continuum edge dominates, correcting a previously reported constant limit. For $N=3$, a transverse contour pinch reduces the spectral integral to one dimension. Assuming that the reduced expansion is complete, in the continuous phase the regulated edge behaves as a discrete state, and the OTOC approaches a pure braiding phase. As we check numerically, the edge block is a free-field correlator in a charge-neutral Weyl frame; this explains the pure phase and is… — Giwan Kim, Masahito Yamazaki — arXiv math-ph / hep-th

item.title: Integrability and closed spacelike extremals of conformal arclength in the Einstein universe
item.description: We study the conformal arclength functional for nondegenerate spacelike curves in the three-dimensional Einstein universe and classify its closed extremals up to conformal equivalence. We show that the extremals are projections of trajectories of a generically noncommutatively integrable Reeb flow. For extremals with nonconstant conformal invariants, closedness forces negative helicity and regular elliptic momentum. We prove that the restricted moment map over the corresponding invariant region defines a nontrivial principal $\mathbb T^3$-bundle, and construct explicit local trivializations that linearize the Reeb flow. This yields explicit parametrizations in terms of elliptic functions… — Emilio Musso — arXiv math.GT / AT / SG / DG

item.title: From Integrability to Chaos in Tensionless AdS3 String Theory
item.description: We study quantum-gravitational corrections to the planar integrable structure of the symmetric product orbifold $\text{Sym}^N(\mathbb{T}^4)$ that is dual to tensionless string theory on AdS$_3\times$S$^3\times \mathbb{T}^4$. We consider the deformation that switches on R-R flux in the bulk, and analyze the associated level spacing statistics. The leading non-planar corrections lift the planar degeneracies and produce signs of random-matrix behavior. Our results provide a controlled example of string interactions driving the onset of quantum chaos. — Matthias R. Gaberdiel, Beat Nairz, Cheng Peng — arXiv math-ph / hep-th

item.title: Black hole binary mergers in dynamical Chern-Simons gravity with regularisation
item.description: We study the non-linear dynamics of Chern-Simons gravity with numerical relativity for the first time. We use the regularisation prescription to obtain a well-posed initial-value formulation in the gauges commonly used in numerical relativity, and we simulate head-on collisions and binary black hole mergers in the regime of validity of effective field theory, extracting the corresponding scalar and gravitational waves. This opens up the possibility to test general effective field theories of gravity, including those with higher-than-second-order equations of motion, with gravitational waves. — Llibert Arest\'e Sal\'o, Maxence Corman, Pau Figueras, \'Aron D. Kov\'acs, Shunhui Yao — arXiv gr-qc / astro-ph.CO / hep-ph / arXiv math-ph / hep-th

item.title: Analytical solution of general interface problems for reaction-advection-diffusion equations
item.description: We obtain novel integral representations, expressed as contour integrals in the complex Fourier plane, for the solution of fully nonhomogeneous interface problems for classical reaction-advection-diffusion (RAD) equations with arbitrary initial data on the line and general interface conditions at the origin. Such problems of applied mathematics emerge in a spectacular variety of physical phenomena in mathematical physics, chemistry, continuum mechanics, biology, pharmacokinetics, as well as mathematical finance. A suitable implementation of Fokas' unified transform method is in force herein, with particular challenges arising due to inclusion in the model of lower-order terms, and the… — Andreas Chatziafratis, Guenbo Hwang, Georgia Karali — arXiv math.AP / CA / PR / DS / arXiv math-ph / hep-th

item.title: Spin-geodesic systems
item.description: We introduce and study a class of geometric dynamical systems on Riemannian manifolds called spin-geodesic systems, in which the motion of a point is coupled to an internal classical spin through a symmetric endomorphism field $B$, the spin-coupling field. These systems may be viewed as $B$-dependent deformations of geodesic motion and have connections with frame flows, magnetic geodesic flows, and nonholonomic rolling systems. We show that every spin-geodesic system admits an equivalent interpretation as a no-slip rolling system in an abstract ambient geometry; when the associated metric connection, determined by $B$, is flat, this construction reduces, under the usual integrability… — Renato Feres, Zijie Hu — arXiv math-ph / hep-th / arXiv math.GT / AT / SG / DG

item.title: Classification of Chern-Simons Couplings and Deformed Pull-Backs on D-Branes
item.description: We establish a framework for classifying higher-derivative Ramond-Ramond (RR) couplings on Dp-branes, focusing on the complete scattering amplitude of a closed-string RR state, a gauge field, and two transverse scalars. The low-energy expansion reveals infinite massless poles and local interaction terms, surpassing standard Myers and Taylor expansions. We propose a higher-class deformation of the pullback using mixed Chern-Simons transgression operators to address these complexities. Our three conjectures are as follows: 1. For fixed field content and derivative order, effective couplings form a finite-dimensional space under stated equivalences. 2. A family of mixed RR, gauge, and scalar… — Armin Hatefi, Ehsan Hatefi — arXiv gr-qc / astro-ph.CO / hep-ph / arXiv math-ph / hep-th

item.title: All-Order Linearized Hydrodynamics of Charged Holographic Plasmas
item.description: We investigate linearized all-order transport in a finite-density holographic plasma described by five-dimensional Einstein-Maxwell-Chern-Simons theory. By retaining the full frequency- and momentum-dependence of the fluid/gravity equations, we determine generalized shear, diffusion, higher-gradient, and chiral-vortical transport functions together with their real-time memory kernels. The different channels exhibit a clear hierarchy of temporal response: the leading shear and diffusion sectors respond promptly, whereas the higher-gradient sectors develop only after a finite buildup time. Remarkably, the chiral-vortical response also shows a finite buildup time despite entering at first… — Karthik R., Shamant Shreedhar Dixit, K. M. Ajith, Kartheek Hegde, Shreyas Punacha, A. Naveena Kumara — arXiv gr-qc / astro-ph.CO / hep-ph / arXiv math-ph / hep-th

item.title: Baker-Akhiezer functions for Koornwinder-van Diejen integrable system
item.description: The Koornwinder-van Diejen integrable system is a counterpart of the trigonometric Ruijsenaars integrable system (associated with the root system $A_n$) for the root system $(C_n^\vee, C_n)$. It depends on the standard Macdonald parameters $q$ and $t$ as well as the Koornwinder (Askey-Wilson) parameters $a$, $b$, $c$, $d$. Different specializations of the parameters connect it to the other classical root systems from the $(C_n^\vee, C_n)$ family. The eigenfunctions of the Koornwinder-van Diejen integrable system are the symmetric Koornwinder polynomials; for certain values of the parameters $t$, $a$, $b$, $c$, $d$ they coincide with the sum over the Weyl group of the Baker-Akhiezer… — Liudmila Bishler — arXiv math-ph / hep-th

item.title: $AdS$ Leading Regge Trajectory from String Field Theory
item.description: We determine the $AdS$ mass of the leading Regge trajectory in superstring backgrounds $AdS_5\times S^5$, $AdS_4\times\mathbb{CP}^3$, and $AdS_3\times S^3\times{\cal M}_4$ with pure Ramond-Ramond (RR) flux for both ${\cal M}_4=S^3\times S^1$ and ${\cal M}_4=T^4$, to the second order in the expansion with respect to the background RR flux by solving the linearized equations of motion in closed superstring field theory. The $AdS_5$ and $AdS_4$ results are in a complete agreement with those obtained from the integrability approach to dual gauge theories, thereby providing a nontrivial check of the holographic duality beyond supersymmetry-protected quantities. — Minjae Cho, Jo\~{a}o Gomide, Jaroslav Scheinpflug, Xi Yin — arXiv math-ph / hep-th

item.title: A spin chain as a deformed conformal field theory: an ODE/IM approach
item.description: The ODE/IM correspondence relates ordinary differential equations to integrable quantum field theories in the continuum. We ask whether it extends to integrable spin chains of finite length $N$. We analyse the twisted XXZ chain at a special anisotropy and twist, focusing on states in its Lee--Yang scaling sector. Their finite-size corrections are expected to come from the Lee--Yang conformal field theory deformed by irrelevant operators, and with the help of the ODE/IM correspondence we make this deformation explicit for the energy and the local conserved charges. Near each of the two edges of the distribution of the Bethe roots, the chain behaves as one chirality of the Lee--Yang theory… — Sujay K. Ashok, Nicol\`o Primi, Roberto Tateo — arXiv math-ph / hep-th

item.title: Extremal Projectors and the Virasoro Algebra
item.description: Extremal projectors are universal operators projecting onto the highest weight space in a representation. Their existence and uniqueness (as formal series) are known for a broad range of Lie superalgebras and quantum groups. We consider a class of Lie superalgebras that contains reductive finite-dimensional Lie algebras as well as the Virasoro algebra. We prove the existence and uniqueness of an extremal projector for this class. The existence proof is given in terms of a recursive algorithm which can be used to compute the coefficients. To illustrate the method, we compute the terms for the Virasoro extremal projector up to order 6. Furthermore, we formulate a conjecture for the… — Jonas T. Hartwig, Sagar Shrivastava — arXiv math.NT / AG / RT / arXiv math-ph / hep-th

item.title: A covariant analysis of massless Dirac fields in LRS spacetimes
item.description: We investigate the massless Dirac field in locally rotationally symmetric (LRS) spacetimes using a covariant spinorial-fluid representation, with the spinor current and spin direction aligned with the LRS frame. When the current has both vorticity and sheet twist, characterized by a constant ratio $\lambda$, the LRS integrability condition relates evolution and propagation derivatives, reducing the field equations to an ordinary differential system that can be integrated exactly. The integrability of the chiral angle forces the heat flux to vanish and the source to saturate the null energy condition along the two radial null directions. A constant boost in the radial Lorentzian two-plane… — Eduardo Bittencourt, Sante Carloni, Giuseppe De Maria, Peter K. S. Dunsby — arXiv gr-qc / astro-ph.CO / hep-ph / arXiv math-ph / hep-th

item.title: Projectivized ASEP-Bethe system and counting solutions
item.description: This paper addresses the problem of counting solutions to the ASEP-Bethe ansatz equations. In an earlier preprint, Brattain, Do, and Saenz presented an algebro-geometric method for counting the number of such solutions. As their method relies on sophisticated machinery, it requires advanced knowledge of algebraic geometry and topology. In this paper, we provide an alternative and simpler method for counting solutions, based on a standard intersection theory on projective varieties. We take a conventional approach in algebraic geometry: ``Projectivize the problem and count degrees.'' We introduce a projectivized version of the ASEP-Bethe equations, whose solution set is realized as a… — Shinsuke Iwao — arXiv math.NT / AG / RT / arXiv math-ph / hep-th

item.title: Nonlinear stability of periodic waves in the Benjamin-Ono equation
item.description: We construct the Lyapunov functional for the periodic waves of the Benjamin-Ono equation based on the conservation of momentum, energy, and a higher-order energy, which exists due to integrability. Positivity of the second variation of the Lyapunov functional for perturbations in Sobolev space $H^1(\mathbb{R})$ is established by utilizing the basis properties of eigenfunctions of the linearized Benjamin-Ono equation in $L^2(\mathbb{R})$. Coercivity of the Lyapunov functional for co-periodic and multiple-periodic perturbations yields the nonlinear orbital stability of the periodic waves in the periodic domain. — Jinbing Chen, Colin Grant, Dmitry E. Pelinovsky — arXiv math.AP / CA / PR / DS / arXiv math-ph / hep-th

item.title: Dirichlet walls beyond JT gravity and their quantum group interpretation
item.description: We canonically quantize sinh dilaton gravity with finite Dirichlet boundary conditions. The reduced phase space is formulated in terms of the length of a two-sided spacelike geodesic in an effective AdS$_2$ geometry and its conjugate momentum. Canonical quantization leads to a finite-difference Schr\"odinger equation whose wavefunctions of the universe are given by $q$-hypergeometric functions. These furnish a quantum deformation of the hypergeometric wavefunctions of JT gravity. We further show that the finite cutoff Hamiltonian derived from the bulk analysis admits a natural interpretation as the reduced Casimir of $U_q(\mathfrak{sl}(2,\mathbb{R}))$ acting on hyperbolic matrix elements… — Luca Griguolo, Jacopo Papalini, Lorenzo Russo, Domenico Seminara, Alex Tarana — arXiv math-ph / hep-th

item.title: Black holes and 2-group symmetry from blackfolds in minimal supergravity
item.description: We investigate the black hole phase diagram of five-dimensional minimal supergravity using the blackfold approach and the framework of generalized symmetries. Starting from supergravity coupled to probe sources, we derive the 2-group (non-)conservation laws, construct the equilibrium action for a two-dimensional 2-group fluid, and compute the associated global conserved charges. We then match the thermodynamics of the general non-extremal black string in the ungauged theory to that of this fluid, organizing the blackfold effective theory and its solutions in terms of symmetry invariants. In the non-extremal ungauged sector, we perturbatively construct new black rings, Saturns, di-rings… — Jay Armas, Giorgos Batzios, Pedro Vicente Marto, Chiara Toldo — arXiv gr-qc / astro-ph.CO / hep-ph / arXiv math-ph / hep-th

item.title: Learning the Anyon Atlas
item.description: We extend our previous search for the modular data of topological quantum field theories in 2+1 dimensions from 22 to 42 anyons, identifying 150,679 new modular data. We do so by adding to our algorithm three rejection gates, two of them based on logistic regression, that discard representations of $SL(2,\mathbb{Z})$ unlikely to yield modular data. We estimate that roughly 80% of the modular data between ranks 23 and 42 has been identified after closing under known constructions. With this data, we find counterexamples to a conjecture of Geiko and Moore that the reality of the higher Gauss sums suffices for time-reversal symmetry in Chern-Simons theories, and propose a refined criterion… — Jonah Berean-Dutcher, Clay Cordova, Julio Parra-Martinez, Richard Tuddenham, Zekai Zhu — arXiv cs.AI / cs.LG / cs.LO (AI for math) / arXiv math-ph / hep-th

item.title: Orbit-averaged spinning and eccentric binary black holes: Hamiltonian and integrability
item.description: For over two decades, the orbit-averaged precession equations of spinning binary black holes at second post-Newtonian order have been a standard model for their spin dynamics. One of their constants of motion, the projected effective spin, underlies the stability analysis of aligned-spin configurations and the construction of analytical solutions. The system is known to be Hamiltonian and integrable, its Hamiltonian being the orbit average of the full post-Newtonian Hamiltonian. Independently, we derive this Hamiltonian from the equations of motion alone, show why the orbit average gives the correct equations, and relate its constants of motion to those of the full system. item.title: Root-of-Unity Limits of Trigonometric qKZ Connections
item.description: Over the field of complex numbers, we study root-of-unity limits of trigonometric qKZ connections associated with tensor products of $U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ Verma modules and of their hypergeometric solutions. As the multiplicative step approaches a primitive $m$-th root of unity and the quantum-group and twist parameters approach $1$, the $m$-step qKZ transport yields, on every fixed-degree subspace,a differential connection. We show that this connection is the pullback of the trigonometric KZ connection under the power map $z\mapsto z^m$, with the KZ parameter rescaled by $m$, and establish formal and $\ell$-adic versions. item.title: UV Bounds on Inflationary Parity Violation
item.description: A question of fundamental interest is whether parity is violated on large scales in the Universe.
